newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada settles Mulroney libel suit - report.
newsitem.headline: Canada settles Mulroney libel suit - report.

text.p: Former Prime Minister Brian Mulroney has reached an out-of-court settlement in his C$50 million ($37 million) libel lawsuit against the Canadian government, the Canadian Broadcasting Corp said on Sunday.

Citing a source close to the case CBC television said the settlement included an "unequivocal apology" from the government for wrongly accusing Mulroney of taking kickbacks in Air Canada's C$1.8 billion ($1.3 billion) purchase of Airbus jets in 1988.

Mulroney's lawsuit centered on a letter sent by Canada's Justice Department to Swiss authorities in September 1995 in which Mulroney was accused of accepting illegal commissions in the Airbus purchase.

The CBC said an official announcement of the settlement was to be made on Monday, the day the unprecendented lawsuit was to be heard in a Montreal court. In the settlement, the government also agreed to pay Mulroney's legal costs of about C$1 million ($740,000), the CBC said.
Government officials and Mulroney's legal team did not return reporters' telephone calls Sunday night to confirm the CBC report.

In a pre-trial hearing last April, Mulroney, who was Conservative prime minister from 1984 to 1993, vehemently denied the government's allegations, accusing the Justice Department and Royal Canadian Mounted Police of "fascism" in their investigation of the Airbus matter.
